name: Acute Transverse Myelitis with Anti-Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein (MOG) Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for MOG Antibody-Associated Disease

criteria.description: Acute onset of bilateral motor, sensory, and autonomic spinal cord dysfunction consistent with transverse myelitis
Presence of serum anti-MOG IgG antibodies detected by cell-based assay
MRI showing longitudinally extensive or short-segment spinal cord lesions consistent with transverse myelitis
Exclusion of alternative etiologies such as multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4 antibody positive), infections, or vascular causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Acute clinical presentation of transverse myelitis with positive serum anti-MOG antibodies and supportive MRI findings, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein are common but not mandatory; anti-MOG antibody testing should be performed using validated cell-based assays.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral motor weakness with rapid progression
searchTerms: rapidly worsening weakness in both sides
fast onset motor weakness both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sensory level deficit corresponding to spinal cord lesion
searchTerms: sensory loss at specific spinal level
sensory deficit matching spinal cord lesion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bladder and bowel dysfunction due to autonomic spinal cord involvement
searchTerms: bladder and bowel problems from spinal cord damage
loss of bladder and bowel control

common.symptomName: Spinal cord pain or radicular pain at lesion level
searchTerms: spinal or nerve root pain at lesion site
back pain radiating from spinal lesion
radicular pain related to spinal injury

common.symptomName: Lhermitte’s sign (electric shock-like sensation on neck flexion)
searchTerms: electric shock sensation when bending neck

occasional.notes: May occur as part of MOG antibody-associated disease spectrum
searchTerms: inflammation of optic nerve causing vision problems
visual disturbances from optic nerve inflammation
optic nerve swelling with vision loss
head pain at beginning of illness

rare.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness requiring ventilatory support

laboratory: Positive serum anti-MOG IgG antibodies by cell-based assay
imaging: Spinal MRI showing T2 hyperintense lesions, often longitudinally extensive
Possible gadolinium enhancement of spinal cord lesions
Brain MRI usually normal or with nonspecific findings
other: Exclusion of AQP4-IgG antibodies to differentiate from neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
Electrophysiological studies may show conduction block or slowed conduction in affected spinal segments

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of AQP4 antibodies instead of MOG antibodies
More severe optic neuritis and spinal cord involvement
Typical brain MRI lesions with periventricular distribution
Oligoclonal bands in CSF more common
Evidence of infectious agent in CSF or blood

redFlags: Rapidly progressive paralysis with respiratory compromise
Loss of sphincter control with urinary retention
Signs of spinal cord compression or vascular ischemia
references: Jarius S, et al. MOG encephalomyelitis: international recommendations on diagnosis and antibody testing. J Neuroinflammation. 2018.
Wingerchuk DM, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology. 2015.
Reindl M, et al. Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibodies in neurological disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2019.
